items.title: OSINTdefender The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted …
items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted inside the internal weapons bay of an F-35C Lightning II with an AIM-120 AMRAAM mounted on the bay door. The Navy describes the AIM-424 as its next-generation, long range air to air missile, intended to give Navy and Marine Corps aviators greater capability against advanced threats.  The internal carriage is particularly significant. Rather than simply adding another externally carried long-range missile, the AIM-424 appears to have been designed around the F-35's limited internal weapons-bay dimensions, allowing the aircraft to retain its low-observable configuration while carrying a substantially longer-range air-to-air weapon.  The missile is still associated with testing and development, and the Navy has released few technical details regarding its range, seeker, propulsion or intended employment. The available imagery does, however, show the AIM-424 being evaluated on both the F-35C and F/A-18E/F, indicating that the weapon is being considered across the Navy's carrier aviation force. items.summary_raw:
Trump posts map showing Hormuz as 'new US territory'

US president Donald Trump has posted a map on his Truth Social account marking the Strait of Hormuz as "NEW U.S. Territory".

It is the second time in a week that Trump has shared the image, but he included no caption or commentary this time.

On Friday, Trump told a public rally that he views Hormuz as "an American territory right now" and vowed Iran cannot be allowed to have a nuclear weapon.

items.title: BIG: Qatar slashed government budgets by up to 30% and cut overseas aid by roughly 85% as the Iran war devastates its LNG-dependent economy.  Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan, the wor…
items.summary_raw: BIG: Qatar slashed government budgets by up to 30% and cut overseas aid by roughly 85% as the Iran war devastates its LNG-dependent economy.  Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan, the world's largest LNG hub, cut export capacity by 17%, with full recovery expected to take 3-5 years.   The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has further crippled exports.   The IMF projects Qatar's GDP will contract 8.6% in 2026.  Goldman Sachs estimates Qatar and Kuwait are losing $1.5-2 billion per week in energy revenue.   Qatar is drawing on its roughly $500 billion sovereign wealth fund to maintain liquidity but is "seriously contemplating" further cuts if the crisis continues.  Source: FT

items.title: Wildfires Continue in Greece, Bringing Destruction and Tragedy
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – Water-dropping aircraft and ground forces managed to bring under control three wildfires in mainland Greece on August 20, as about half the country faced a category-3 risk on a 5-notch scale. Earlier in the week two wildfires broke out nearly simultaneously on the island of Salamina near Piraeus. The situation turned tragic, with two people, believed to be an elderly couple, found dead in the Peristeria area. Eight people suffered burns, while there were reports of homes being completely engulfed in flames. On Aug. 20 the Fire Service said four aircraft flew sorties to help 35 firefighters contain a blaze near the village of Kremasti in the Sparta region of the southern Peloponnese. Two more wildfires coursing through forest and farmland near the villages of Palamas in the central Karditsa region and Paralimni in the northern Serres area were brought under control. For Aug. 20, civil protection authorities have set most of the country on a category-3 risk level, including nearly the entire Peloponnese, central Greece with the Greater Athens region and the island of Evia, northwestern Greece, Crete and nearly all the Aegean Sea islands.

items.title: Trump Is Destroying America’s Greatest Strategic Asset
items.summary_raw:
For eighty years, America's greatest strategic advantage was not its aircraft carriers, nuclear weapons, economy or even the dollar. It was its allies. Russia has satellites and dependents. China has partners and clients. Iran has proxies. America built something none of them could reproduce: alliances with countries that actually wanted to be our allies. They trusted us because, despite our mistakes and occasional arrogance, they believed Washington would ultimately take their interests into account.

items.title: NEW: Germany is planning nearly €12 billion for a new long-range strike arsenal to deter Russia.  The four-layered plan starts with cheap, mass-producible cruise missiles as early …
items.summary_raw: NEW: Germany is planning nearly €12 billion for a new long-range strike arsenal to deter Russia.  The four-layered plan starts with cheap, mass-producible cruise missiles as early as 2027, including Ukraine's FP-5 Flamingo with 3,000 km range at roughly one-fifth the cost of a Tomahawk.   US Tomahawk missiles with Typhon launchers follow by end of the decade.   The most expensive element is a joint UK-Germany program developing stealth cruise missiles and a hypersonic glide weapon exceeding 2,000 km range, targeted for the mid-2030s.  Documents describe the capability as enabling strikes "far into the rear area of an adversary" while staying "below the nuclear threshold."   Source: Politico

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ 🔻Global oil prices rose on Friday following US President Donald Trump's threat to impose economic sanctions on countries that provide assistance to Iran. Brent crude oil reached $94.39 per barrel, an increase of 61 cents per barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude also rose to $87.06, an increase of 23 cents. According to a Reuters report, Brent crude rose by more than 6%, and US crude rose by more than 5% this week. Analysts say that the new US threat to increase economic pressure on Iran and its trading partners has heightened concerns about declining oil supplies in the coming weeks. At the same time, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly below its usual levels. Data from Kepler, a company specializing in ship tracking, indicates that only seven commercial vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, a figure that represents half the number recorded the previous day. Before the start of the American attacks on Iran at the end of February, about one-fifth of the world's supply of oil and liquefied natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Wildfire Breaks out in Thanos on the North Aegean Island of Limnos
items.summary_raw:
MYRINA – A state of alert was declared on Friday, August 21 on the island of Limnos in the northern Aegean Sea after a wildfire broke out in the Thanos area, on the southern side of the island, prompting a major mobilization of the Fire Service and Coast Guard. The fire broke out at around 2:30 PM in low vegetation and, as it spread, it became necessary to evacuate residents and beachgoers from areas near the fire front. A particularly large-scale operation took place at Thanos Beach, where dozens of people, including elderly people and children, had become trapped. Under the coordination of the Operations Center of the Hellenic Coast Guard, a total of 59 people were evacuated by sea and safely transported to the port of Myrina.

The post Wildfire Breaks out in Thanos on the North Aegean Island of Limnos appeared first on The National Herald.

ATHENS. Turkey’s latest moves in the Aegean are not simply another episode in the long chain of Greek-Turkish disputes. Ankara’s successive challenges to Greece’s marine parks, its Maritime Spatial Planning framework and, most recently, the Special Spatial Planning Framework for Renewable Energy Sources point to a more systematic effort to extend its longstanding claims into every new activity involving the maritime space. The most troubling aspect is not so much Ankara’s reaction to Greek initiatives as the revival of its “gray zones” theory. Turkey’s Foreign Ministry, followed by its Defense Ministry, referred to “geographical formations whose sovereignty has not been transferred to Greece through international treaties.” Athens responded in unusually strong terms, calling the claims “unfounded, completely unacceptable and rejected,” and stressing that the status of sovereignty in the Aegean has been definitively established by international treaties.

items.title: Trump Warns of ‘Economic D-Day’ Against Iran, but Tehran Is Well Acquainted With Sanctions
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK (AP) — Nearing the six-month mark of the Iran war and facing diminishing stockpiles of key weapons, the Trump administration is touting a crushing financial campaign against Tehran, promising an “economic D-Day” against a country that has so far withstood nearly five decades of punishing American sanctions. With sparse details, President Donald Trump announced this week that the U.S. would be imposing an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation on Iran, aiming to force its leadership to cave to demands to end its nuclear program and fully reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz to oil and natural gas tankers. It reflects the dire reality Trump faces with an increasingly unpopular war he can't seem to end just months before pivotal midterm elections that will decide whether his Republican Party keeps control of Congress. Whether out of desperation or strategy, the president is refocusing America's might on bringing Iran to its knees through an accelerated sanctions campaign against one of the most economically penalized countries in the world.

items.title: Proposed London datacentre will have annual carbon footprint of 27,000 flights to New York
items.summary_raw:
Exclusive: Planning documents show datacentre in North Ockendon would be incompatible with UK net zero targets

A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 27,000 flights from London to New York, planning documents show.

The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”.

items.title: OSINTdefender Two F-16AM Fighting Falcons with the Romanian Air Force were scrambled early Thursday to investigate an unidentified naval surface drone spotted near the Neptun Deep …
items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender Two F-16AM Fighting Falcons with the Romanian Air Force were scrambled early Thursday to investigate an unidentified naval surface drone spotted near the Neptun Deep Project, a major European offshore natural gas field off the coast of Romania in the Black Sea.   On approach, the drone - believed to be of Russian origin - was determined to be an active threat, with one of the F-16s using its M61A1 Vulcan Six-Barrel Gatling Gun to target and destroy the explosive-laden surface drone, roughly 80NM east of the Russian Black Sea coastal city of Constanța.  Romanian President Nicușor Dan blamed the incident on Russia, stating in a post online: “I strongly condemn the intensification of these types of irresponsible incidents on the part of the Russian Federation.” While European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described it as part of an “escalating campaign of threats” against the European Union. tweet

items.summary_raw:
Administration’s plan to scrap drilling-free buffer zone around New Mexico site prompts scrutiny from Unesco

The Trump administration’s push to expand oil and gas extraction across the US is set to bring drilling near cherished natural and cultural sites, raising alarm among conservationists and prompting questions from the UN’s heritage body.

Unesco said it had received information on the administration’s plan to scrap a drilling-free buffer zone around the Chaco Culture national historical park in New Mexico, a world heritage site and one of the most important cultural areas in the US. A Unesco spokesperson said it had procedures regarding “potential threats” to a world heritage property and was awaiting a response from the federal government as to its impact.

items.title: OSINTdefender Another day of heightened aerial activity near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.  Thanks to reporting from @thewarzonewire's @Haltman, we now know the activity is p…
items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender Another day of heightened aerial activity near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.  Thanks to reporting from @thewarzonewire's @Haltman, we now know the activity is part of a U.S.-led NATO exercise that also includes a ground component involving Polish armed forces, although their specific role has not been disclosed.  Several U.S. Air Force and NATO tankers are operating in refueling racetrack orbits over Polish airspace, while a NATO E-3 AWACS is orbiting just north of the tanker tracks.  A U.S. Air Force EA-37B "Compass Call II" electronic-warfare aircraft has also made the trip into the area again, this time flying directly from Chania, Greece, before operating near Kaliningrad.  A NATO official told The War Zone that the exercise is not in response to recent Russian military activity or rhetoric. However, comments from a Polish official appeared to indicate that deterrence is part of the broader purpose of the exercise.  The activity remains notable given the concentration of airborne early warning, electronic warfare, ISR and aerial refueling capabilities operating in close proximity to Kaliningrad. tweet

items.title: Ankara Revives ‘Gray Zones’ Claims Over Greece’s Renewable Energy Plan
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Turkey has revived its longstanding claims over the status of parts of the Aegean, this time objecting to Greece’s new spatial planning framework for renewable energy projects. The latest move came from Turkey’s Defense Ministry on Thursday, one day after the Foreign Ministry had already challenged the Greek framework, which entered into force Wednesday and also covers the Aegean Sea. Turkey’s Defense Ministry said the Greek plan would have no legal consequences for Ankara and would not alter Turkey’s established position on what it describes as outstanding Aegean issues. In doing so, Ankara again referred to geographic formations whose sovereignty, in Turkey’s view, was not transferred to Greece through international treaties. The wording effectively brings the so-called “gray zones” issue back to the forefront. Greece has consistently rejected the Turkish claim, maintaining that the sovereignty of the Aegean islands is established by international treaties and international law.

items.title: Israeli defence minister warns Turkey against 'threatening its security'
items.summary_raw:
Israeli defence minister warns Turkey against 'threatening its security'

Israel's defence minister said that president Recep Tayyip Erdogan is "dragging Turkey into dangerous adventures in Syria," indicating that Ankara risks consequences for its ties with Damascus. 

"Israel will not allow any actor to threaten its security,"  Israel Katz said in a post on X.

"It would be better for Erdogan to continue his detached-from-reality, fanciful rhetoric against Israel in the Turkish Grand National Assembly than to attempt to test Israel's determination to defend itself."

items.title: Weatherwatch: Climate crisis fuelling steep fall in migratory bird numbers
items.summary_raw:
Many species under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the planet’s largest mass-migration systems

It may still feel like summer, but in the world of birds, autumn migration is already well under way. Cuckoos and swifts have already left us, and while swallows and many species of warbler will not depart our shores until September, many species of Arctic-breeding waders have begun to stop off at our coastal marshes to refuel for their long journey south.

This year, however, there could be fewer than usual. A review by the British Trust for Ornithology, working with other international conservation organisations, has found that more than half of these global travellers are suffering major declines in numbers – a worrying downward trend. Many of those under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the largest mass-migration systems on the planet.

items.title: From bone-dry to soaked to the bone, welcome to the age of climate whiplash | Aditya Chakrabortty
items.summary_raw:
This punishingly hot and dry summer will probably be followed by another wet winter. But it’s nothing compared with what Britain will endure in years to come

This summer could be the hottest, driest and deadliest in English history. Successive heatwaves have so far claimed almost 3,000 lives. This is a major concern for Gustaf Hugelius, a professor at the Bolin Centre of Climate Research at Stockholm University, Sweden, and a leading authority on the risks from thawing tundra and peatlands. In this Q&A, he explains why the world should pay attention.

Trump disclosed today that North Korea possesses "57 very powerful nuclear weapons," adding that the arsenal "shouldn't have been allowed to happen." The figure is notable because the U.S. government does not publicly disclose a precise number for North Korea's nuclear stockpile; outside estimates have generally placed it in the roughly 50–90 warhead range.  The disclosure comes days after Trump ordered Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to substantially reduce U.S.-South Korean military exercises, arguing that the drills are too costly and send an "inappropriate and hostile" signal to North Korea, which he described as "unthreatening and respectful."  The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise subsequently began but was shortened by six days, with Seoul announcing that it would conclude Friday rather than continue through its originally scheduled period.  Trump has also said he intends to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un later this year, potentially marking another effort to revive the diplomacy that stalled after the 2019 Hanoi summit. items.title: Proving the Negative: Three Warnings from Arms Control for the Age of AI
items.summary_raw:
In early 1963, a single number characterized the difference in the positions of the United States and the Soviet Union on a comprehensive nuclear test ban. Nikita Khrushchev had proposed three on-site inspections each year. Washington was asking for seven. Other differences remained, including inspection procedures and treaty language. But the difference mattered: Seismology could not always distinguish an underground test from an earthquake, and inspections created both assurance and opportunities for espionage.Neither number had been delivered by a technical expert wielding a seismograph. items.title: Carbon pollution has fuelled ‘massive expansion’ of marine heatwaves in Europe, study finds
items.summary_raw:
Hottest periods this year in most sea regions would have been ‘virtually impossible’ in a preindustrial climate

Carbon pollution has fuelled a “massive expansion” of marine heatwaves in Europe this summer, research has found, with some waters recording temperatures 6C higher than normal.

The hottest fortnights of this year would have been “virtually impossible” in a preindustrial climate in three of the four sea regions studied, according to analysis by World Weather Attribution, while in the Celtic region, which covers much of the water around the British Isles, heat hit levels that used to strike just once a century.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender The U.S. Army is preparing to stand up a new Patriot air-defense battalion on Guam in October, adding another layer to the island’s growing integrated air and missile defense network, according to reporting from TWZ.  The new 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment (3-43 ADA) will combine Patriot with Indirect Fire Protection Capability (IFPC)/Enduring Shield, giving Guam layered protection against ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones. About 120 soldiers are already on the island, with the weapon systems expected to arrive over the following months.  The move is significant given Guam’s role as a major U.S. air and naval hub in the Western Pacific and its vulnerability to Chinese ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missile threats. The broader Guam Defense System is also incorporating new sensors, including the LTAMDS and AN/TPY-6, and ground-based launchers capable of supporting SM-3/SM-6 interceptors.  But the timing also highlights a broader problem: the Army needs more Patriot battalions at the same time its existing force is already heavily strained. The Army currently has 15 operational Patriot battalions and has discussed adding at least three

items.summary_raw:
Almost 45m acres of national forests could be potentially opened to road construction, drilling and logging

The Trump administration said on Tuesday it plans to rescind the “roadless rule” that has protected old growth forests in the US for 25 years, potentially opening up almost 45m acres of national forests to road construction, drilling and logging.

Conservationists had feared the announcement was coming since last summer after Brooke Rollins, Trump’s secretary of agriculture, targeted a rule brought in by Bill Clinton’s administration, describing it as “overly restrictive” and an “absurd obstacle” to development.

items.summary_raw: Syria publicly confirmed possessing nuclear material left over from the Assad regime.   IAEA chief Grossi said "tons of nuclear materials that could be put to bad use" were found at an undeclared site.  Syria voluntarily informed the IAEA in July and granted inspectors access.   Foreign Minister al-Shaibani said the material will remain in Syrian custody under IAEA safeguards, adding that Syria "affirms its sovereign and legal right to a peaceful nuclear program."  The material is linked to the Al-Kibar reactor that Israel destroyed in 2007, believed to have been built with North Korean assistance.   Grossi said Syria has regained its place as a fully compliant state:   We are now turning the page on the past.

items.title: England’s ancient oak trees dying in extreme hot and dry weather
items.summary_raw:
Woodland Trust says trees struggling in drought stress, with older ‘survivors’ disproportionately affected

England’s ancient oak trees are dying in the summer’s extreme heat and dry weather, according to the Woodland Trust, with trees and ecosystems unable to adapt fast enough to the changing climate.

The heatwaves across much of Europe this summer have had a notable impact on crop growth and plant health. To cope with the extreme conditions, many trees are undergoing “early autumn”, wilting and losing their leaves early.

items.title: EMBCA Hosts Event on the Istanbul Pogrom of September 6-7, 1955, on Sept. 6
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – The East Mediterranean Business Culture Alliance (EMBCA) presents ‘Before and After the Istanbul Pogrom of September 6-7, 1955: The Destruction of the Hellenic (Rum) Community of Turkey’ on Sunday, September 6, 2 PM EDT/ 9 PM Athens (EEST) online. The discussion will be introduced and moderated by Lou Katsos, President of EMBCA. The distinguished panel will include Dr. Alexandros K. Kyrou, Professor of History and Director of the Program in East European and Russian Studies at Salem State University; Dr. Konstantinos Tsitselikis, Professor of Human Rights and International Organizations at the University of Macedonia; Dr. Elizabeth H. Prodromou Professor in the International Studies Program at Boston College; Prof. Dr. Johannes Niehoff-Panagiotidis of the Freie Universitat Berlin; Dr. Harry G. Dimopoulos, International Businessman and 1955 Pogrom Survivor; and Stelios Taketzis, Producer and former Executive Director of Cosmos FM.

items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇦⚡️ Ukraine is beginning to move critical energy infrastructure underground, with frontline Zaporizhzhia becoming the first city to build underground protection for key power facilities as Kyiv prepares its grid for further Russian attacks.   According to regional military administration chief Ivan Fedorov, underground protective structures are being constructed at two substations, while transformers at other critical facilities are being reinforced with massive concrete shelters. More than half of the region’s key transformers have already received protective structures, reducing their vulnerability to Russian missiles and drones.   This is Ukraine adapting its infrastructure to a long war. Instead of relying solely on scarce and expensive air-defense interceptors, Kyiv is increasingly making the targets themselves harder to destroy. If the Zaporizhzhia model proves effective and expands nationwide, Russia will have to spend considerably more weapons to achieve the same level of damage to Ukraine’s energy grid, precisely the kind of unfavorable exchange Kyiv needs ahead of future winter strike campaigns.  See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

French vegetable production is down by “a very significant extent” compared with previous years, French growers have said, with shortfalls put at 25% for courgettes, 35% for lettuces, 40% for peas, 60% for broccoli and 50% to 100% for artichokes.

items.summary_raw:
Pentagon signs multibillion-dollar Tomahawk deal amid missile shortage concerns

The Pentagon announced a $22.9bn contract with Raytheon on Monday to accelerate deliveries of Tomahawk missiles, amid reports that US missile stocks have been strained by the war with Iran.

Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the deal would speed up deliveries “at unprecedented speed” to meet current operational demands.

A recent analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that US stocks of Patriot and THAAD interceptors have been cut by roughly half or more since the conflict with Iran began in late February.

Trump contradicts Vance on top US goal in Iran war

US President Donald Trump said preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon is Washington’s “number one Goal”, appearing to contradict Vice President JD Vance, who last week said keeping oil and gasoline prices low for Americans was the administration’s top priority.

“The number one Goal is, and always will be, that Iran cannot have, in any way, shape, or form, a Nuclear Weapon,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Vance told Fox News last week that the administration’s first goal was to “keep oil and gasoline cheap for Americans”, with ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon coming second.

items.title: Trump Orders Pentagon To Scale Back Joint Exercises With South Korea
items.summary_raw:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon on Sunday to scale back annual joint military exercises with South Korea, saying the ally declined to help with the war against Iran and citing his good relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un. Trump said in a social media post that the exercises, which began Monday, are not only costly but “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, which he said “has been unthreatening and respectful” during his time in the White House.
“Therefore, and based on the fact that it is too late to cancel, I have instructed Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises!” Trump wrote. The president added that he recently asked South Korea’s president if they would join the U.S. in the “denuclearization” of Iran, “and they said, ‘No thanks!’”

The post Trump Orders Pentagon To Scale Back Joint Exercises With South Korea appeared first on The National Herald.

The prime minister of Iraq's Kurdistan Regional Government, Masrour Barzani, said on Monday that Iranian drones targeted his office and the home of the head of the Kurdistan region’s Security and Intelligence Agency.

“Following an investigation by the Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Unit, my personal office and the home of the head of the Security and Intelligence Agency were targeted by Iranian drone attacks earlier today,” he said in a post on X, adding that the attacks were “reckless and unacceptable”.

He called the strikes a “dangerous escalation” and said they posed a direct threat to the security and stability of Iraq's Kurdish region.

The semiautonomous region has faced missile and drone attacks since the US-Israel war on Iran

Netanyahu has insisted that any settlement must ensure Hamas is “genuinely disarmed”.

Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, met Hamas’s new leader Khalil al-Hayya in the Egyptian city of el-Alamein on Sunday, AFP reported.

The US envoy urged Hamas to take “concrete, verifiable steps” and conveyed that “Gaza can never again be a source of terror for Israel”, while the group reiterated its commitment to the proposed plan, the report said.

items.title: Greek Foreign Ministry: Turkish “Marine Parks” Illegal, Create No New Facts in Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Greece has sent a clear message to Ankara that the designation of Turkish “national marine parks” in areas beyond Turkish territorial waters has no legal effect and cannot create faits accomplis, following the publication of the relevant Presidential Decrees in the Turkish Official Gazette. Under the Presidential Decrees of 15 August, Turkiye designated two “national marine parks” in the northeastern Aegean and the Eastern Mediterranean, whose boundaries extend beyond Turkish territorial waters. In a statement, the Greek Foreign Ministry described the establishment of the parks as unlawful insofar as they cover international waters, stressing that, under the Law of the Sea, no state has the right to unilaterally establish marine protected areas outside its national jurisdiction. At the same time, Athens underlined that the Turkish marine parks are also unlawful insofar as they extend into the Greek continental shelf. Consequently, the Foreign Ministry stressed, the Turkish action “produces absolutely no legal effect”, either with regard to international waters or Greek sovereign rights over the continental shelf.

items.title: Iran's FM Spox. Esmail Baghaei:  There is no provision titled “60-day deadline” in the text of the memorandum of understanding.   The Islamic Republic of Iran never formulates its …
items.summary_raw: Iran's FM Spox. Esmail Baghaei:  There is no provision titled “60-day deadline” in the text of the memorandum of understanding.   The Islamic Republic of Iran never formulates its policies under pressure, ultimatums, or time deadlines.  What was stipulated in the memorandum was merely a 60-day period for discussions on two issues: “lifting sanctions” and “the nuclear issue.”   If no result was reached, this period could be extended.  Due to the gross and widespread violation of the June 18 memorandum of understanding by the United States only a few weeks after it was signed, no talks were ever initiated.   Consequently, the issue of a 60-day deadline became entirely moot.

items.title: Lala weakens to tropical storm as it lashes Hawaii with heavy wind and rain
items.summary_raw:
Hurricane Lala downgraded after skirting Big Island as one person dies and 183,000 still without power

Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm on Sunday after skirting Hawaii without making landfall, but it wasn’t done punishing the Big Island with hurricane-force gusts. Total rainfall of nearly 3ft (1 meter) was expected on the higher windward slopes, turning rivers into raging torrents and threatening mudslides.

The Hawaii governor, Josh Green, said at least one person died in a car accident in the South Point area of the Big Island, where more than 100 homes were destroyed. A little over 183,000 utility customers remained without power across Hawaii by Sunday mid-afternoon, according to the utility tracker PowerOutage.us. At least three hospitals were operating on generator power, and 19 roofs were lost, Green said.

items.title: Florida sets record for sea turtle nests but Trump move could stall recovery
items.summary_raw:
Loggerhead turtles abound this season but rollback of Endangered Species Act protections could threaten future

Wildlife groups in Florida are celebrating record numbers of sea turtle nests this season, but experts warn Donald Trump’s recent gutting of the Endangered Species Act (ESA) could reverse decades of their recovery from the edge of extinction.

With more than two months of the summer nesting season still to run, loggerhead turtles have already made 13,770 nests, hundreds more than recorded in any previous year, along an 8.5-mile stretch of shoreline monitored by the Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach, on Florida’s Atlantic coast.

Savaş Çakar, a Turkish crew member, was killed when the coal-carrying vessel was hit.   His brother Abbas Çakar, a journalist, said the message doubled his anger and vowed to pursue accountability.  Ukraine has not officially confirmed or denied the email.   The family is reportedly preparing an ICC complaint.
